statement_record.book: The category 4 (the four-element ordinal) is a preorder, so all four triangular faces of its cube of arrows commute; it is free on the quiver . -> . -> . -> . ; hence a diagram of shape 4 in C is exactly a sequence of three composable morphisms f, g, h together with the composites gf, hg, hgf, associativity supplying commutativity of the remaining faces.
statement_record.intree: Proset P builds a category out of any preorder with hom-setoid `fun _ _ => True` (thin, so any two parallel paths are ≈); Omega is the ordinal ω in that style with hom := le_t; FreeOnQuiver G has hom := tlist edges (finite composable paths) and UniversalArrowQuiverCat asserts that a quiver homomorphism G ⇨ QuiverOfCat C extends to a unique functor FreeOnQuiver G ⟶ C.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the general machinery is present (an ordinal/preorder IS a thin category; the free category on a quiver has paths as morphisms and functors out of it correspond exactly to quiver maps, i.e. to the generating arrows), but the SPECIFIC shape category 4 does not exist in the tree at all, and no statement identifies a diagram of shape 4 with three composable morphisms. statement_record.book: Let f_1,...,f_n be a composable path. If some contiguous sub-composite f_k...f_i equals g_m...g_1 for another composable sequence, then f_n...f_1 = f_n...f_{k+1} g_m...g_1 f_{i-1}...f_1. Proof: composition is well defined, so pre- and postcomposing equal arrows with the same sequences yields equal arrows. This is the principle underlying most diagram chases.
statement_record.intree: `compose_respects` is a mandatory field of `Class Category`: composition is Proper for ≈ in both arguments, so `f ≈ f' → g ≈ g' → f ∘ g ≈ f' ∘ g'`; together with `comp_assoc`/`comp_assoc_sym` any contiguous sub-composite can be bracketed out and replaced by an ≈-equal one.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Riehl's n-ary path statement is exactly the iterated binary congruence: pre- and post-composing both sides of the hypothesis is two applications of `compose_respects`, and isolating the contiguous block f_k...f_i inside the whole path is `comp_assoc`. The library is if anything more general, since ≈ (not equality) is the relation and the congruence is a stated law rather than a consequence of well-definedness.

statement_record.book: For a triple of morphisms with the displayed domains and codomains in which f is an isomorphism, the left-hand triangle commutes if and only if the right-hand triangle (with f replaced by f⁻¹, reversing that edge) commutes; explicitly h = gf if and only if h f⁻¹ = g. Dually, for a triple in which k is an isomorphism the analogous two triangles are equivalent.
statement_record.intree: `iso_cancel_spine_tf : (X ∘ to i) ∘ from i ≈ X` and `iso_cancel_spine_ft : (X ∘ from i) ∘ to i ≈ X` — the two one-sided cancellation identities; plus `iso_to_epic` / `iso_to_monic`, which say an isomorphism can be cancelled from either side of an equation of composites.

Class ZeroObject (C : Category) := { zero_terminal : @Terminal C; zero_initial : @Initial C; zero_coincide : @initial_obj C zero_initial ≅ @terminal_obj C zero_terminal }.

statement_record.book: In a category C: an object i is INITIAL if for every object c there is a unique morphism i -> c; dually t is TERMINAL if for every c there is a unique morphism c -> t. An object both initial and terminal is a ZERO OBJECT.
statement_record.intree: `Class Terminal` packages the object `terminal_obj`, the morphism `one : x ~> terminal_obj` for every x, and its uniqueness `one_unique : f ≈ g`; `Initial C` is notation for `@Terminal (C^op)` with the C-side projections `initial_obj`, `zero : initial_obj ~> x` and `zero_unique : f ≈ g`; `Class ZeroObject` bundles a Terminal and an Initial together with `zero_coincide : initial_obj ≅ terminal_obj`.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, with two faithful setoid/constructive rephrasings. (a) 'unique morphism' is split into existence (the field `one`/`zero`) and uniqueness up to the hom-setoid relation ≈ rather than equality — the standard faithful rendering in this library. (b) `ZeroObject` requires the initial and terminal objects to COINCIDE UP TO ISOMORPHISM (`zero_coincide`) rather than to be literally the same object, which is setoid-honest and equivalent in content to Riehl's 'both initial and terminal'.

statement_record.book: The full subcategory of C spanned by its terminal objects is either empty or a contractible groupoid (a non-empty category with exactly one morphism in each hom-set, equivalently equivalent to 1; also called chaotic); in particular any two terminal objects are uniquely isomorphic. That subcategory is moreover replete. Dually for initial objects.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition Replete : Type := ∀ (x : C) (ox : sobj S x) (y : C) (f : x ≅ y), { oy : sobj S y & shom S ox oy (to f) ∧ shom S oy ox (from f) }.

statement_record.book: (Footnote 45) A subcategory D of C is REPLETE if for every isomorphism f : c ≅ d of C with d in D, the object c, the morphism f and its inverse f⁻¹ all belong to D as well.
statement_record.intree: `Replete : Type := ∀ (x : C) (ox : sobj S x) (y : C) (f : x ≅ y), { oy : sobj S y & shom S ox oy (to f) ∧ shom S oy ox (from f) }` — over `Record Subcategory` (Construction/Subcategory.v:31), whose fields are the object subcollection `sobj`, the morphism subcollection `shom`, and closure under composition and identities.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Riehl assumes one endpoint of the isomorphism lies in D and concludes that the other endpoint, the isomorphism, and its inverse lie in D; the in-tree definition assumes the source endpoint lies in D and concludes the same three things (the object `oy`, the morphism `to f`, and `from f`). The two orientations agree because ≅ is symmetric in-tree (`iso_sym`, Theory/Isomorphism.v:156), so quantifying over all isomorphisms out of a selected object is the same condition as quantifying over all isomorphisms into one. The Type-valued sigma/conjunction packaging is the library's standard constructive rendering of 'belongs to D'.

statement_record.book: Let f_1,...,f_n and g_1,...,g_m be composable sequences with dom f_1 = dom g_1 and cod f_n = cod g_m. If that common codomain is a terminal object, or that common domain is an initial object, then f_n...f_1 = g_m...g_1. Proof: the uniqueness clause of Definition 1.6.14.
statement_record.intree: `one_unique {x} (f g : x ~> terminal_obj) : f ≈ g` and `zero_unique {x} (f g : initial_obj ~{C}~> x) : f ≈ g`.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, in fact intree-stronger in form: Riehl quantifies over composites of composable sequences, the library over ARBITRARY parallel morphisms with terminal codomain (resp. initial domain), of which those composites are instances — the chain packaging carries no extra content since a composite is just a morphism. Both of Riehl's clauses (terminal codomain, initial domain) are covered, the second by the library's duality (`Initial C` is notation for `@Terminal (C^op)`). The corollaries `one_comp : one ∘ f ≈ one` (Structure/Terminal.v:119) and `zero_comp : f ∘ zero ≈ zero` (Structure/Initial.v:124) are the two-arrow special case, and the ZeroObject file's `zero_mor_left`/`zero_mor_right` are the same principle for tunnelled zero morphisms.

statement_record.book: A CONCRETE CATEGORY is a category C equipped with a faithful functor U : C -> Set, thought of as taking each object to its underlying set. Faithfulness says parallel morphisms inducing the same function of underlying sets are equal, so being a morphism is a PROPERTY of the underlying function.
statement_record.intree: `Class Faithful (F : C ⟶ D) := { fmap_inj : fmap[F] f ≈ fmap[F] g → f ≈ g }` is the faithfulness half, verbatim (injectivity of the hom-map, phrased with ≈). `ev1_Faithful : Faithful ev1` is the only in-tree instance whose codomain is `Sets` — i.e. the only in-tree exhibition of a category as concrete.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the ingredient (`Faithful`) matches Riehl exactly, but the DEFINITION being catalogued — the bundling of a category with a chosen faithful functor to Set — is never made. No `Concrete`/`ConcreteCategory` class or record exists, so 'C is concrete' cannot be stated as a hypothesis or concluded as a theorem anywhere in the library, and the gloss 'being a morphism is a property of the underlying function' has no formal counterpart.

statement_record.book: Every category listed in Example 1.1.3 is concrete, but multi-sorted cases need care: for Quiver and Ch_R the obvious forgetful functors sending a quiver to its set of vertices, or to its set of arrows, are NOT faithful. An alternative functor V + A : Quiver -> Set sending a quiver to the disjoint union of its vertex and arrow sets IS faithful, so Quiver is concrete.
statement_record.intree: `ev1_Faithful : Faithful ev1` for `ev1 : Models T Sets ⟶ Sets` establishes that the category of Sets-models of a Lawvere theory has a faithful underlying-set functor (under an explicit reachability hypothesis). `Mon_Forget_Faithful` / `Comon_Forget_Faithful` establish the analogous fact for categories of monoid/comonoid objects, but with codomain the ambient category C rather than Sets.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on both clauses. For the first clause the in-tree witness covers ONE family (Sets-models of a Lawvere theory, and even there only under `reach`), not Riehl's specific list — none of Set, Top, Set_*, Group, Ring, R-Mod, Ch_R, Graph, Man, Meas, Poset is shown concrete in-tree, and most of those categories do not exist in-tree at all. For the second clause there is nothing: `QuiverCategory` exists (Construction/Free/Quiver.v:358) but the library defines no functor from it to `Sets` whatsoever, so neither the failure of faithfulness for the vertex-only/arrow-only functors nor the faithfulness of V + A can even be stated.
